h: Grid roads, redways and a putter in hand
p: Milton Keynes was designated as a new town in 1967, and it was planned from scratch with its famous grid road system and a network of shared cycle and footpaths known as the redways. Handy to know if you're visiting with bikes or scooters, as the redways make it surprisingly easy to get between parks, lakes and leisure spots without dealing with the roads.

For a crazy golf trip, the practical stuff is simple. A round usually takes about an hour, and a little longer with a big group. Get there ten minutes before your slot, decide on any house rules before the first putt (is there a maximum number of shots per hole? there should be), and let the little ones have a go at keeping score. They'll be strict, you'll see.

MK is packed with other leisure, so it's easy to build a whole day. Xscape, with its indoor real-snow slope, is right by the centre, and Gulliver's Land is a theme park aimed squarely at younger children. If you're already planning a trip to Bletchley Park, the National Museum of Computing sits on the same site and is brilliant for anyone into old machines and how computers began.

Football fans can catch MK Dons at their stadium in Denbigh, and for a quieter wander, Campbell Park in the middle of town has views across the city and some public art dotted about. Pair a round of putting with a couple of these and the whole family will sleep well on the way home.
